question: Does the intra-tool-call heterogeneity finding in 7335a82 replicate on an independent cohort, or is it a property of one trace?
finding: Replicates. The headline quantity is nearly identical across cohorts: a single call-level limit wastes 48.8% of the RSS resource-time envelope on SWE277 and 48.1% on SWE100. Multi-clause fraction (48.4% vs 44.3%), null-label fraction (53.3% vs 51.8%) and p90 dispersion (586x vs 461x) all agree closely.
the_one_statistic_that_does_not_replicat: The peak/min MEDIAN moves from 36.0x to 13.2x. It is computed over only 768 and 246 usable multi-clause calls and is sensitive to the smallest clause in each call, so it is the least stable of the reported statistics. The envelope figure, which is duration-weighted, is the one to quote.
limitations: Both cohorts are the same benchmark, agent scaffold and model, so this is replication across traces, NOT across workloads. It does not establish that the property holds for non-SWE agents.
Both inherit the 29.4% clause resource-time coverage gap documented in 9d1db84.
